issues.description: The problem statement gives contradictory guidance about the stock attribute: it instructs students to initialize attributes (including stock) in the instance constructor (lines describing default initialization in the constructor), but elsewhere explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (class-level) and final. A static final field cannot be properly initialized in an instance constructor, so students may be confused about whether stock should be an instance or class attribute and where to initialize it.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: either (A) make stock an instance (non-static) final field and instruct students to initialize it in the (no-arg) constructor, or (B) require stock to be static final and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem statement to remove the contradictory instruction about initializing a static field in the instance constructor.

issues.description: The template and the solution use different getter names for the StockIngredient name field: the template's StockIngredient defines getIngredientName() and Stock.findStockIngredient(...) calls getIngredientName(), whereas the solution's StockIngredient defines getName() and its Stock.findStockIngredient(...) calls getName(). This naming inconsistency between template and solution can confuse students comparing the two codebases or when adapting code from one to the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent across template, solution, and problem description. Prefer a single name (e.g., getName()) and update both StockIngredient and any calls (Stock.findStockIngredient and other usages) in template and solution to use that same getter name so students are not confused by differing implementations.

issues.description: The getter for the ingredient name in StockIngredient is named differently between template and solution. The template's StockIngredient exposes getIngredientName(), while the solution's StockIngredient exposes getName(). Corresponding usages in Stock.findStockIngredient also call different getters (template uses getIngredientName(), solution uses getName()). This inconsistent identifier naming for the same conceptual property (the ingredient name) across artifacts can confuse students when they map the problem requirements to the provided code and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the getter name for the ingredient's name across template and solution. Either rename the template's getIngredientName() to getName() and update all calls (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) accordingly, or change the solution to use getIngredientName() everywhere. Ensure the same identifier is used in both StockIngredient and its usages so students can map the concept consistently.
